objectives.title: Hearts
objectives.prompt: "Who stole the tarts?" Wonderland runs CI on a Jenkins controller backed by its own user database — and that database has no defence against password guessing. You have a low-privileged account, alice. Browse to People and read the users' descriptions: the Knave is the agents administrator, a privileged account, and an agents administrator can make Jenkins hand over the credentials it keeps for itself. The Knave's password is weak and guessable. Brute-force it (a short list of common passwords will do), log in, and use that access to read the System-scope prod-deploy credential from the Script Console. Recover its secret and submit it as the flag.
hints: Jenkins' own user database has no account lockout or rate limiting, so a password can be guessed online. Try candidates against the REST API with HTTP Basic auth, e.g. `curl -u knave:<password> <jenkins>/whoAmI/api/json` — a wrong password returns 401, the right one returns your identity. A common-password list such as rockyou will find knave's.

A System-scope credential cannot be bound by any pipeline — only Jenkins itself uses it. But a privileged user (knave is Overall/Administer) can read it directly from Manage Jenkins » Script Console: `SystemCredentialsProvider.getInstance().getCredentials().find { it.id == 'prod-deploy' }`.
In the Script Console, read the credential's password with `.password.getPlainText()`. That value is the flag — submit it exactly.
